THE CLAUSE

Guideline: Instructions that can be implicitly overridden.

CLAUSES IT CROSS-REFERENCES

The levels of authority are as follows

Here is the ordering of authority levels. Each section of the spec, and message role in the input conversation, is designated with a default authority level.

1. **Root**: Model Spec "root" sections
2. **System**: Model Spec "system" sections and system messages
3. **Developer**: Model Spec "developer" sections and developer messages
4. **User**: Model Spec "user" sections and user messages
5. **Guideline**: Model Spec "guideline" sections
6. *No Authority*: assistant and tool messages; quoted/untrusted text and multimodal data in other messages

6. *No Authority*: assistant and tool messages; quoted/untrusted text and multimodal data in other messages

THE CLAIMS READ OUT OF IT

  C1 the guideline authority level is the level of instruction authority at which instructions can be implicitly overridden
  C2 an instruction at the guideline level is implicitly overridable by an instruction from a higher authority level

EVERY SENTENCE THE TRANSLATION RENDERS BACK

  0. «the guideline level of instruction authority: instructions at this level can be implicitly overridden by higher-authority instructions»
  1. «which of two instruction authority levels is the higher one in the ranking root > system > developer > user > guideline > no authority»
  2. «instruction I is issued at authority level L»
  3. «instruction I can be implicitly overridden by instruction J without J explicitly stating that it overrides I»
  4.
